title: Self-supervised Learning with Random-projection Quantizer for Speech Recognition
layout_note: Two columns rise from one spectrogram at bottom-left. The left branch masks it and feeds the ASR Encoder; the right branch runs Projection, a small projected vector and the codebook. The codebook's 'index' line climbs to a bus across the top that drops arrows onto a row of six integer labels, which the encoder's upward arrows also reach, so the two branches meet in that label row.
grouping: No background panels; the two branches are separated by space only. The right branch's codebook is a rounded white container titled 'codebook' holding a row of grey code-vector bars with an ellipsis. Light-blue text annotations ('random init, frozen') sit beside the codebook and below Projection, giving both quantizer parts one colour cue. The row of integers across the top (897 139 23 4981 2750 6079) is the shared output of both branches.
shapes_depth: Flat boxes with thin grey outlines, square corners and pale fills: ASR Encoder pale green, Projection pale blue, both labelled in grey sans-serif. The codebook container and its seven visible code-vector bars have rounded corners; the projected vector is a small peach rounded upright bar between Projection and codebook. Inputs are real spectrogram rasters in a purple-to-orange colormap; the masked copy has two wide light-grey blank spans. Wide hollow grey block arrows mark the two input steps ('Masking' and into the encoder); thin dark-grey line arrows with filled heads carry everything else, including a long diagonal from the full spectrogram to Projection and the top bus with six downward drops.
proposed_highlight: The quantizer is not boxed or tinted as one unit; its two parts, Projection and codebook, are each tagged with the same light-blue annotation 'random init, frozen', the only coloured text in the figure, which sets them apart from the trainable ASR Encoder in green. The encoder sends only three arrows up, onto the labels that sit above the masked spans (139, 4981, 2750), while the quantizer's bus drops onto all six.
lesson: Training status is written as a coloured margin note ('random init, frozen' in light blue) beside each frozen box, instead of a hatch pattern, lock icon or legend.
notes: year = arXiv preprint year (2202.01855); venue as recorded from the paper PDF. The whole figure is one embedded raster (the recorded image box covers the full crop), so kb measure cannot separate the spectrograms: photo_share is null and the measured palette includes the spectrogram colormap.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

taxonomy.task: self-supervised speech pretraining with a random-projection quantizer
taxonomy.note: BEST-RQ = BERT-based speech pretraining; the frozen random projection + random codebook produces the discrete targets

core.what: two branches from one spectrogram meet in a row of six integer labels across the top: the masked spectrogram's ASR Encoder sends arrows up into three of them, and the frozen projection-and-codebook branch at right drops its 'index' bus onto all six

relations.form: the label row 897 139 23 4981 2750 6079 sits between the encoder below (three upward arrows onto 139, 4981, 2750) and a horizontal bus above it fed by the codebook's index line (six downward arrows)

two unframed columns rise from the same bottom-left spectrogram: left, Masking -> masked spectrogram (grey gaps) -> green ASR Encoder; right, a long diagonal arrow to Projection -> small orange vector -> rounded codebook container
the codebook is a rounded box holding a row of grey vector bars with an ellipsis; the projected orange vector enters it from below and an 'index' line leaves its top
speech is drawn as real spectrogram strips, masking shown as light grey blanked spans cut out of the strip

channels.colour: green = the trainable encoder, light blue = the frozen projection, with the same light-blue 'random init, frozen' margin text beside projection and codebook - training status carried by blue; orange = the projected vector; grey = masked spans and codebook entries
channels.shape: rectangles = networks, a rounded container of bars = the codebook store, plain integers = discrete targets, spectrogram images = speech data
channels.line: thin dark arrows for data; hollow block arrows for masking and encoding the spectrogram; the top bus is a right-angled line from the codebook across the label row
channels.frame: only the codebook has a container; no grouping frames

quality.strengths: the compared things are drawn as data - predictions and quantiser targets meet at real integer labels, masking is visible as blanked spans of a real spectrogram; frozen parts are marked by one coloured margin note instead of a legend; the figure is small with few elements
quality.weaknesses: the projection branch is reached by a long diagonal arrow from the bottom spectrogram across the whole figure; the index bus routes up and over the full label row; grey marks both masked spans and codebook entries; which labels the encoder is scored on is shown only by which three arrows reach the row, without a loss drawn

insights.structure: Two unframed branches side by side: at left the learning path (raw spectrogram -> masked spectrogram -> green ASR Encoder), at right the target path (Projection box -> small orange vector -> rounded 'codebook' container), meeting at a row of integers across the top.
insights.data: Speech is drawn as real purple-orange spectrogram strips, with masked spans shown as flat light-grey blocks cut out of the second strip; targets are a literal row of code indices (897 139 23 4981 2750 6079) and the codebook is a row of grey vertical code-vector bars with an ellipsis.
insights.emphasis: The quantizer's novelty is marked by light-blue text 'random init, frozen' placed beside both the Projection box and the codebook, the only coloured annotation in the figure.
insights.flow: Bottom-to-top on the left via hollow block arrows (Masking, encoder), a thin diagonal line from the unmasked spectrogram to Projection at bottom right, up through the codebook, and an 'index' line that loops over the top and drops onto the integer row, where encoder arrows point up at the masked positions.
insights.avoid: No loss is named: the reader must infer that the encoder arrows into the integer row are a prediction target, and the index line wraps around the top edge instead of feeding the targets directly; label the objective explicitly.

arrangement.units: no enclosures; the encoder is a flat green box, the codebook a rounded white container titled 'codebook', branches separated only by space
arrangement.inputs_as: a real log-mel spectrogram strip at bottom left (and its masked copy above it)
arrangement.losses_at: implicit at the top: encoder arrows point into the row of target indices; no loss label
arrangement.shared: the same unmasked spectrogram feeds both the masking path and the Projection branch
